name: Ortho rule
summary: A connection between two H-boxes that are controlled by a bit and its negation can be removed.
description:
Two H-boxes that are connected to the same Z-spider, one of them via a NOT, are 'orthogonal': for every value of the Z-spider exactly one of them is active. The rule says that a wire between two such H-boxes can be replaced by plugging a phase-free Z-state into each of them (up to a scalar).

This rule is part of every complete axiomatisation of the ZH-calculus, but is arguably the hardest to motivate. The 2021 completeness paper shows that it can be replaced by the two simpler rules [Z(π) copies through an H-box](../zh-h-box-z-pi-copy/) and [AND of a copied bit](../zh-dedup/).
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
